appraisal_events.evidence: je ne pus pas attraper son regard... aucun son, aucun mouvement ne trahirent que M. de Charlus eût entendu ma question... ce fut à elle seule qu'il adressa la parole pendant cette soirée et pas une seule fois à moi
appraisal_events.explanation: Charlus pointedly refuses to meet the narrator's eye, disowns having invited him, ignores his direct question, and speaks only to the grandmother all evening, a sustained cold exclusion of the narrator.

appraisal_events.evidence: Ah! c'est une très bonne idée que vous avez eue de venir, c'est charmant... Mme de Villeparisis... parut soudain avoir trouvé à ma grand'mère de nouvelles qualités et ne cessa de lui faire fête
appraisal_events.explanation: Charlus's conspicuous warmth toward the grandmother, crediting her (not himself) with the idea of coming, visibly raises her currency with Mme de Villeparisis, who begins to make a fuss over her.

appraisal_events.evidence: Dame, ils n'ont pas cet air de race, de grand seigneur jusqu'au bout des ongles, qu'a mon oncle Palamède
appraisal_events.explanation: Saint-Loup singles out Charlus as possessing an aristocratic bearing that other Guermantes lack, a comparative distinction.

status_effects.explanation: Despite personally inviting him hours earlier, Charlus now shuts the narrator out of the conversation entirely, addressing only the grandmother the whole evening.
Charlus's visible favor toward her is registered and echoed by Mme de Villeparisis, who suddenly makes much of her.
Saint-Loup's comparison marks Charlus as distinctly possessing the aristocratic bearing other Guermantes lack.

ambiguities: The narrator's long fascinated description of Charlus's eyes and face as enigmatic, dangerous, and 'tragic' does not resolve into a clear positive or negative evaluation and is left as unsettled mystery rather than a scored movement.
